title: New-Member Transition Desk Reference: Continuity-of-Care Quantity Limit Authorizations
content:
Under the Utilization Management Program, a new member whose prior pharmacy carrier's approval for an acute migraine drug (sumatriptan, Nurtec ODT or Ubrelvy) is on file — that is, whose case for the drug relies on the prior carrier's approval — receives a continuity-of-care quantity limit authorization for that drug.

## Governing rule

A continuity-of-care authorization is put in force for the prior carrier's approval on file for the drug. The quantity per rolling 30 days it carries is the quantity the Utilization Management Program determines for continuity-of-care quantity limit authorizations. The authorization runs from the review program effective date for the package's continuity approval days and is granted only inside the continuity window.

## What a grant records

One grant records one new quantity limit authorization for the drug that came about through continuity of care, linked to the member's case that carries the prior carrier's approval, with the quantity per rolling 30 days it covers and its first and last days in force. No review decision is recorded. Afterwards the member's authorizations list it.

## How it is invoked

The tool is `grant_continuity_authorization_38eb93b7`, an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks it and then calls it. The grant is complete when the receipt shows status "in_force".

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `customer_id` | the customer reference number of the member, as read from the customer profile lookup | identifier |
| `review_program_id` | the reference number of the member's Utilization Management Program, as read from the review program lookup | identifier |
| `source_case_id` | the reference number of the opening of the member's case that relies on the prior carrier's approval, as read from the review case lookup | identifier |
| `drug_name` | the drug the authorization covers | one value of the drug list below |
| `approved_quantity_per_30` | the quantity of the drug per rolling 30 days the authorization covers | decimal units, up to 3 decimals |
| `effective_date` | the first day the authorization is in force | YYYY-MM-DD |
| `expiration_date` | the last day the authorization is in force | YYYY-MM-DD |

**`drug_name` values:** `atorvastatin`, `lisinopril`, `metformin`, `sertraline`, `levothyroxine`, `sumatriptan`, `oxycodone-acetaminophen`, `insulin glargine-yfgn`, `Lantus`, `Eliquis`, `Xarelto`, `Jardiance`, `Ozempic`, `Mounjaro`, `Wegovy`, `Zepbound`, `Trelegy Ellipta`, `Breztri Aerosphere`, `Nurtec ODT`, `Ubrelvy`, `Humira`, `adalimumab-adaz`, `Dupixent`, `Skyrizi`, `Rinvoq`, `Enbrel`, `Biktarvy`, `Ibrance`.

## Receipt

A successful call returns `authorization_id` (the reference number of the new authorization), `drug_name`, `auth_basis` (always `continuity_of_care`), `approved_quantity_per_30` (up to 3 decimals), `effective_date` and `expiration_date` (YYYY-MM-DD) and status "in_force".

*Hypothetical illustration:* a grant for `Ubrelvy` with `approved_quantity_per_30` 18 returns an `authorization_id`, `auth_basis` `continuity_of_care` and status "in_force".
